div.head: ECf retr 32.2
div.ab: Teutonici et Frisones et Flandrenses consules suos maregraue, quasi maiores dominos uel bonos pacificos, uocare consuescunt.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 654 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page; the words in bold are the Retractator’s changes to ECf, as Liebermann prints them.

note.seg: Markgraf erlischt als Titel in Flandern 1119 und kommt in Frisland 1046—1103 vor (Warnkönig Flandr. RG. I 256; Waitz Dt. Verf.-G. VII 79). Retr. schlimmbessert, als wären Frisones et Fl. nicht Teutonici, und als hätten die Deutschen nicht auch Grafen

Markgraf dies out as a title in Flanders in 1119 and occurs in Frisia 1046–1103 (Warnkönig, Flandr. RG. I 256; Waitz, Dt. Verf.-G. VII 79). The Retr. makes it worse in correcting it, as if the Frisians and Flemings were not Teutonici, and as if the Germans did not also have counts

Verf. identificirt falsch in Markgraf, das er in Franz. Aussprache hörte, graf mit gerefa und die erste Silbe mit Engl. (oder ähnlichem Niederdeutschen) mare (maior) oder mit mære, welches aber eher berühmt, hehr als gut bedeutet

in Markgraf, which he heard in French pronunciation, the author wrongly identifies graf with gerefa, and the first syllable with English (or similar Low German) mare (maior) or with mære, which however means famous, exalted rather than good

div.ab: The Germans and the Frisians and the Flemings are accustomed to call their earls (consules) maregraue, as it were greater lords or good peacemakers.
